newsitem.title: UK: Halifax, Alliance & Leicester to join FTSE 100.
newsitem.headline: Halifax, Alliance & Leicester to join FTSE 100.

text.p: Two recently floated former building societies, Halifax Plc and Alliance & Leicester Plc, will replace two smaller companies from the FTSE 100 share index on June 23, the FTSE Actuaries UK Indices Committee said on Wednesday.
The two banking groups will replace drugs firm Smith & Nephew Plc and retailer Burton Group Plc, the committee said in a statement.
Smith and Nephew and Burton Group will both drop into the FTSE-250 share index, the committee announced in its quarterly shake-up.

Halifax and the Alliance and Leicester, which both converted to banks and joined London's bourse over the past two months, easily qualify for inclusion in the elite ranks of Britain's biggest publicly quoted companies.
Halifax has a market capitalisation of around 18.8 billion pounds($30.8 billion) and is Britain's third largest bank. Alliance and Leicester comes in at around 12.4 billion pounds.($20.3 billion)
In contrast, Smith & Nephew and Burton each have a market capitalisation of some 1.9 billion pounds.

A company qualifies for automatic inclusion in the FTSE 100 if it ranks among the top 90 in terms of market capitalisation at the close of business on one of the four quarterly days on which the index constituents are revised.
It replaces the lowest ranking index constituent.
The significance of being included in the FTSE 100 is that institutions running funds tracking the index must build up holdings in those companies on course to get in and sell those that drop out.
The latest additions will further raise the presence of financials in the index, with the flotation of insurer Norwich Union and the Woolwich Building Society still to come.
